mainTopic: The cistern of עולי בבל: partnership, ברירה, and acquiring a found object for a friend; then a new משנה on produce that follows its owner's תחום
overview: The amud opens by finishing a source that רבא quotes against רב נחמן. The source is about people who made a חרם vow against benefiting from each other. It says they may still use things belonging to עולי בבל, such as a cistern in the middle of the road, but not things owned by their city. רבא asks: if that cistern is owned by all Jews as partners, a משנה in נדרים forbids partners under such a vow from using a shared cistern. The first answer is that washing is indeed forbidden, but drawing water is allowed because each person draws from his own share. That answer relies on ברירה. The גמרא then proves from a משנה about brothers, the קלבון and מעשר בהמה that רב נחמן rejects ברירה. So the גמרא gives a new explanation: everyone agrees the cistern is הפקר, and the dispute is whether picking up a found object for a friend acquires it for him. Finally, a new משנה teaches that produce kept in another city follows its owner's תחום, and the owner's own עירוב lets it be brought to him.

steps.title: Vows of חרם between two people
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source rules on one-sided and two-sided vows of חרם. It says both parties may use property of עולי בבל but not property of their city.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'You are forbidden to me as חרם,' the one who made the vow is forbidden. If he says 'I am forbidden to you and you to me,' both are forbidden to benefit from each other. They are permitted in things belonging to עולי בבל, but forbidden in things belonging to their own city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the source that רבא quotes as the basis for his challenge. Here it states the key ruling: two people under a vow may still use things belonging to עולי בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things belonging to עולי בבל are treated as public, so using them is not taking benefit from the other person. Things belonging to the city are jointly owned by its residents, so each person would be using the other's share. This permission is the point רבא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow-language that forbids something like a consecrated item
The person who makes the vow
Those who came up from Babylonia; their items count as public property of all Jews
That city; property jointly owned by its residents

phrases.english: 'You are hereby forbidden to me as חרם' —
the one who vowed is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He forbade the other person to himself, so he may not benefit from him.

phrases.english: 'I am forbidden to you and you to me' —
both are forbidden to benefit from one another,
and they are permitted in things of those who came up from Babylonia,
but forbidden in things of that city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source that רבא began quoting on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People forbidden to each other by a vow may use property of עולי בבל but not property of their city.

steps.title: Examples of public items versus city items
steps.stepSummary: The source lists which items count as belonging to עולי בבל and which belong to the city. A cistern on the road is listed as an item of עולי בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the things of עולי בבל: the Temple Mount, the chambers, the courtyards, and a cistern in the middle of the road. These are things of that city: the street, the synagogue, and the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The source gives examples of each category. The cistern in the middle of the road is the detail רבא is about to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the road cistern is listed among the items of עולי בבל, the vow-makers may use it. That raises a question for רב נחמן, who treats such a cistern as owned jointly by all Jews as partners.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple Mount
Chambers on the Temple grounds
Temple courtyards
A cistern in the middle of the road, a public water pit

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן דְּבָרִים שֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָבֶל:
phrases.english: And these are the things of those who came up from Babylonia:
the Temple Mount, the chambers, and the courtyards,
and a cistern in the middle of the road.
phrases.notes: This is the item רבא's challenge focuses on.

phrases.english: And these are things of that city:
the street, the synagogue, and the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן דְּבָרִים שֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two categories named in step 1, setting up רבא's attack.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A road cistern belongs to the category of עולי בבל and is permitted to the vow-makers.

steps.title: If the cistern is jointly owned, why is it permitted?
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if a public cistern is owned by partners, a משנה in נדרים should forbid the vow-makers from using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a cistern belongs to partners, why is it permitted? But we learned: partners who vowed not to benefit from one another are forbidden to enter the shared courtyard to wash in the cistern!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now finishes his challenge to רב נחמן. If the road cistern is a partnership of all Jews, two partners under a vow should be forbidden to use it, yet the source permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treats a cistern of עולי בבל as jointly owned property. The משנה in נדרים says partners under a mutual vow may not use their shared cistern, because each would benefit from the other's share. So רב נחמן's view seems to contradict the source that permits the road cistern.

keyTerms.meaning: A cistern owned by partners
Why?
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
They vowed against deriving benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not why public property is permitted. רבא is asking how the cistern can be both a partnership, as רב נחמן says, and also permitted, since partners under a vow may not use shared property.

phrases.english: And if you say a cistern is a partners' property,
why is it permitted?
But didn't we learn:
partners who vowed not to benefit from one another —
are forbidden to enter the courtyard
to wash in the cistern!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בֵּירָא דְשׁוּתָּפֵי הוּא, אַמַּאי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the permission from steps 1-2 to attack רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a cistern of עולי בבל is jointly owned by partners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partners under a mutual vow may not use a shared cistern, yet the source permits the vow-makers to use the road cistern. So that cistern must not be a partnership.

steps.title: Washing is forbidden; the source permits only drawing water
steps.stepSummary: Washing really is forbidden. The source permits only filling water, since each person is seen as drawing from his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: For washing, it is indeed so. But what case are we dealing with here? Filling: each one fills from his own share.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge. He agrees that washing in the cistern is forbidden, and explains that our source only permits drawing water from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing uses the whole body of water, including the other partner's share, so it is forbidden. When a person draws water, the water he takes is considered his own portion all along (a form of ברירה), so he takes nothing from his partner. Both sources are now consistent, and the cistern can still be a partnership.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so
With what case are we dealing?
To fill, meaning to draw water
This one from his own share

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא answers this way: washing in a shared cistern is forbidden because it uses the partner's water, but drawing is permitted because each draws from his own share. This answer depends on ברירה. Steps 5-8 show that רב נחמן rejects ברירה, and step 9 replaces this explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer depends on viewing drawn water as retroactively designated to the person drawing it. This idea of designation within shared property ties back to the larger topic of how far items may be carried on יום טוב.

phrases.english: To wash — indeed, so (it is forbidden),
and here, with what are we dealing —
with filling (drawing water),
this one fills from his own (share)
and that one fills from his own (share).

steps.triggerLanguage: לִרְחוֹץ הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by narrowing the case of the source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the permission covers drawing water, not washing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to permit all use of the road cistern, which contradicts the rule for partners.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only drawing is permitted, because each person draws his own share. Washing remains forbidden, as the משנה in נדרים says.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן really hold that ownership can be clarified retroactively?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב נחמן holds יש ברירה. It begins its challenge by quoting a משנה about brothers, the קלבון surcharge, and מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רב נחמן really hold that there is ברירה? But we learned in a משנה: brothers who are partners pay the קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה. When they are obligated in מעשר בהמה, they are exempt from the קלבון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא doubts the previous answer, which relied on ברירה, and starts building a challenge by quoting a משנה. This step is the setup: the משנה is quoted now, and the explanation that makes it a problem comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer only works if each partner's share can be seen as his own from the beginning, which is ברירה. The משנה describes two states for brothers. Partners pay the קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה. Brothers still holding an undivided inheritance are treated as one owner, so they are obligated in מעשר בהמה and exempt from the קלבון.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was 'really' someone's from the start.
'But didn't we learn in a משנה?' The formula for opening a challenge from a משנה.
Brothers who are partners: they inherited together, divided, and then joined their property again.
A small surcharge coin added to the half-shekel Temple donation.
The animal tithe: every tenth newborn animal is set aside. It does not apply to animals owned by partners.

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה describes two different situations. Brothers who divided and then rejoined are 'partners' (קלבון yes, מעשר בהמה no). Brothers who never divided are like one owner (מעשר בהמה yes, קלבון no). Do not mix the two up.

phrases.english: And does Rav Nachman hold that there is retroactive clarification?
phrases.notes: The question targets the previous answer, which assumed each person draws from his own share.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: brothers who are partners,
when they are obligated in the kalbon surcharge,
they are exempt from the animal tithe.
phrases.notes: Partners are exempt from the animal tithe.

phrases.english: And when they are obligated in the animal tithe,
phrases.notes: This is the case where they never divided, so the estate counts as one owner.

phrases.english: they are exempt from the kalbon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב נַחְמָן יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברירה assumption behind the answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's apparent reliance on יש ברירה (each partner draws from his own share).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The laws of brothers who inherit, divide, and rejoin depend on whether their shares count as theirs from the start. This משנה, together with how it is explained, will be used to show that רב נחמן does not hold of ברירה.

steps.title: רב ענן: the משנה speaks of brothers who traded kids for lambs
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן limits the משנה's case. The divided-then-rejoined brothers count as new partners only when one took kids and the other took lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ענן said: The משנה taught this only when they divided kids against lambs and lambs against kids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב ענן's explanation of the משנה, which narrows when the brothers count as ordinary partners. This continues building the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose one brother took young goats and the other took lambs of equal value. Then neither one received a piece of what they shared; it is like each one bought something from the other. Because of that trade, when they rejoin they are a brand-new partnership: they pay the קלבון and are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this in the case of...' A formula that narrows a teaching to a specific case.
Young goats (kids).
Lambs.
Corresponding to, or in exchange for.

phrases.english: And Rav Anan said:
They taught this only where they divided
phrases.notes: This narrows the משנה's ruling about partners.

phrases.english: kids against lambs,
and lambs against kids.
phrases.notes: This kind of split works like a purchase or trade between the brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב עָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and narrows the משנה quoted in step 5, as part of the same challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers are treated as new partners only when their division was an exchange of different kinds of animals (kids for lambs).

steps.title: An even split means each share was his from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן adds the other side. If the brothers split kids against kids and lambs against lambs, each share is seen as his from the moment of inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they divided kids against kids and lambs against lambs, we say: this is his share that came to him from the first moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן finishes his explanation by describing an even split, where each brother's share is seen as his from the very beginning. The גמרא is still setting up its challenge to רב נחמן, and that challenge continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When each brother takes the same kind of animal, we treat his portion as having been his from the moment their father died. That is the ברירה idea. So if they rejoin, they return to being one inheritance: they are obligated in מעשר בהמה and exempt from the קלבון. This sharp line between an exchange and an even split is what the גמרא will use to test רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is his share that reaches him,' meaning the portion that was always meant to be his.
From the first moment, meaning from the time of the inheritance.

steps.whatToRemember: An exchange of kids for lambs works like a purchase, so the brothers become new partners. An even split of kids for kids uses ברירה, so each share was his from the start and the estate stays one unit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for how ברירה works in dividing an inheritance. It frames the test of whether רב נחמן holds יש ברירה.

phrases.english: But if they divided kids against kids
and lambs against lambs,
phrases.notes: Each brother took an equal share of each kind of animal.

phrases.english: one says: this is his share
that came to him from the first moment for this.
phrases.notes: This is ברירה: the share counts as his retroactively, from the time of inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ענן's statement by giving the contrasting case of an even split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an even split, each brother's portion is considered his from the time of inheritance (ברירה), so rejoined brothers are again treated as one estate.

steps.title: רב נחמן rejects retroactive designation even in an even split
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that even when the brothers split kids against kids and lambs against lambs, we do not say each share was his from the start. So he does not hold יש ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said: Even if they divided kids against kids and lambs against lambs, we do not say, 'This is the share that was coming to him from the very first moment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in step 5. It quotes רב נחמן himself and shows that he does not accept ברירה, even in the easiest case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן said that an even split (kids for kids, lambs for lambs) lets us say each brother's share was always his. רב נחמן disagrees even in that case. So רב נחמן clearly does not hold יש ברירה, and the earlier explanation of the cistern dispute, which depended on ברירה, no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: Young goats (kids)
Lambs
Against, matched with
From the first moment, here meaning from the time of the inheritance

steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out the ברירה-based explanation of the cistern argument and forces the גמרא to find a new one.

phrases.english: But Rav Nachman said:
Even if they divided kids against kids
and lambs against lambs,
one does not say: this is his portion
phrases.notes: This is a rejection of ברירה.

phrases.english: that was coming to him from the first moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָלְקוּ גְּדָיִם כְּנֶגֶד גְּדָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב ענן's statement in step 7 and completes the challenge from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier explanation that the cistern dispute depends on ברירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב נחמן rejects ברירה even in an even split, his position in the cistern dispute cannot rest on ברירה.

steps.title: New explanation: the argument is about picking up a found object for a friend
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the public cistern is ownerless. The dispute is really whether someone who picks up a found item for his friend acquires it for that friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that the cistern is ownerless. Here they argue about someone who picks up a found object for his friend. One Sage holds the friend acquires it, and the other Sage holds the friend does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its old explanation and offers a new one for the argument about drawing water for another person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cistern water is now treated like a found object (מציאה) from הפקר, so ברירה is no longer relevant. רב נחמן holds that the friend acquires the water, so it has the friend's תחום. רב ששת holds the friend does not acquire it, so it stays with the drawer's תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownerless property
Picking up a found object on behalf of one's friend
He acquired it
One Sage holds

steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation of the cistern dispute is not about partnership or ברירה. It is about whether a person can acquire ownerless water for someone else by picking it up for him.
steps.confusionAlert: The second אֶלָּא here means 'but' (here they argue about something else). It does not start another rejection.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
that it is an ownerless cistern,
but here
they disagree about one who picks up a found object for his friend.
One Sage holds: the friend acquires it,
and the other Sage holds: he does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּירָא דְהֶפְקֵרָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 8 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the dispute around a different legal principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depended on whether the cistern is jointly owned and on ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cistern is ownerless, and the dispute is about acquiring a found object for one's friend.

steps.title: New משנה: produce kept in another city
steps.stepSummary: If a person's produce is in another city, people from that city may not bring it to him, even if they made an עירוב. But if he made an עירוב himself, his produce has the same range he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person's produce was in another city, and the people of that city made an עירוב so they could bring him some of it, they may not bring it to him. But if he made an עירוב himself, his produce is like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new משנה about how far produce may be carried on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce has the same תחום as its owner. The townspeople's own עירוב does not help, because the produce cannot go past its owner's limit. Once the owner makes an עירוב that lets him reach that city, the produce gets that same range and can be brought to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (abbreviation of מתניתין)
An arrangement that extends how far a person may walk on שבת or יום טוב
His produce
Like him, meaning the produce has the same תחום as its owner

steps.whyThisMatters: It applies the rule that objects follow their owner's תחום to a case where the owner is far from his belongings.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One whose produce was in a different city
and the people of that city made an עירוב
in order to bring him some of his produce,
they may not bring it to him.
But if he himself made an עירוב,
his produce is like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיוּ פֵּירוֹתָיו בְּעִיר אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the cistern discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce follows its owner's תחום. Others' עירוב does not help, but the owner's own עירוב extends the produce's range.
